## 固定收益開場主論述

美國服務業需求轉強、民間聘僱展現韌性，加上油價再度上漲，使聯準會仍有升息可能，美債於6月3日走跌。10年期殖利率上升5.2個基點至4.496%，創兩週最大升幅；5年期上升4.7個基點至4.217%，2年期上升3.9個基點至4.083%，30年期則上升3.6個基點至4.993%。

2年至10年期曲線小幅陡峭化，反映本輪重新定價由實質利率主導，而非長期通膨補償升高。10年期實質殖利率上升6.1個基點至2.104%，10年期損益兩平通膨率反而下降0.9個基點至2.392%。2s10s曲線擴大1.3個基點至41.3個基點；由於30年期公債表現優於10年期券，2s30s則幾乎持平於91個基點。

5月數據顯示需求延續，卻未消除就業標題數字之下的疲弱訊號。ADP公布民間就業增加12.2萬人，略高於經濟學家預期。ISM服務業指數隨後由53.6升至54.5，高於調查預估的53.7，商業活動與新訂單均加速。不過，就業指數仍處於萎縮區間的47.9；另一份標普全球調查則顯示服務業僅微幅成長，就業流失速度為2020年5月以來最快。

通膨細項使較強的經濟活動數據仍足以牽動利率。ISM價格指數由70.7升至71.3；聯準會褐皮書也顯示，能源成本已在美國多數地區傳導至運輸、包裝、食品雜貨與肥料。WTI原油上漲2.41%至$96.02，布蘭特原油上漲1.89%至$97.81，部分逆轉市場先前因期待中東達成和解而出現的緩和走勢。

對政策立場表態最明確的是達拉斯聯準銀行總裁Lorie Logan。她是FOMC具投票權的委員，曾反對4月聲明所呈現的寬鬆傾向。Logan表示，通膨趨勢似乎正朝2%區間中段發展，而非回到2%；同時，勞動市場大致平衡、金融環境仍然寬鬆，因此2026年稍後可能需要升息。紐約聯準銀行總裁John Williams的立場較不具方向性，認為目前政策校準適當，近期沒有升息或降息的必要。

最終，美債殖利率全面但有序上升，並未伴隨通膨補償再次走高，也未出現全面避險潮。標普500指數下跌0.74%，那斯達克100指數下跌0.29%，VIX上升1.84%至16.06，半導體指數則上漲1.39%。美元升值0.31%，黃金下跌1.17%，上市投資級、高收益與新興市場債券基金跌幅介於0.22%至0.37%。市場對升息的疑慮並未消退，但強勁服務業需求與就業萎縮之間的落差，使後續官方非農就業與通膨報告的重要性超過單一強勁標題數字。

## 服務業需求推升實質殖利率

在美國數據公布前，油價已經回升，伊朗衝突迅速和解的前景也轉趨不確定，美債因而率先走跌。ADP估計5月民間雇主增加12.2萬名員工後，殖利率進一步上升；在4月職缺數高於預期之後，這項數據再度顯示勞動需求已趨穩定。

ADP數據不足以證明就業全面加速，卻降低了勞動市場突然轉弱、迫使聯準會暫時擱置高通膨顧慮的可能性。道明證券利率策略師Molly Brooks表示，這份數據進一步印證勞動市場趨穩；即使官方非農就業成長低於正常水準，只要疲弱程度還不足以讓市場將焦點從通膨移開，也未必會引發大幅行情。

ISM服務業報告進一步支持需求仍強的論點。整體指數上升0.9點至54.5，高於調查預估的53.7；商業活動指數由55.9升至57.7，新訂單指數由53.5加速至57.3。這些升幅顯示，擴張並非僅由供應商交貨放緩或庫存累積所造成。

不過，庫存的貢獻異常顯著，指數由53.1躍升至62.5，追平歷史最高紀錄；供應商交貨指數則由56.8降至55.2。這種組合顯示，即使最終經濟活動仍然穩健，部分企業也可能因供應情勢不明而預先備貨。庫存累積目前有助於支撐產出韌性，但若家庭需求減弱，這些存貨能否全數維持仍有疑問。

就業分項則發出重要的反向訊號，由48.0小幅降至47.9，持續低於50的榮枯線。換言之，訂單與商業活動轉強之際，服務業就業仍在萎縮。這項落差對聯準會十分重要：官員可以認定當前需求仍具韌性，卻不能據此推論整體經濟的聘僱正在重新加速。

標普全球服務業終值調查更為疲弱。商業活動指數由51.0降至50.7，略低於50.9的初值，顯示成長幅度極為有限。就業減少速度為2020年5月以來最快，企業樂觀程度降至2022年10月以來最低，海外需求則創2022年11月以來最大降幅。新業務恢復成長，但這份調查並未呈現與ISM同等廣泛的擴張。

因此，兩份服務業調查提供的並非重複確認，而是不同角度的修正。ISM顯示國內活動與訂單加速，兩份調查卻都指向就業疲弱。標普全球並發現投入成本通膨升至5個月高點，ISM價格指數也升至71.3。兩者的共同訊息是：聘僱轉弱尚未明確降低企業成本壓力。

4月工廠訂單則提供較強的硬數據。訂單在3月增幅修正為1.8%後，再成長4.8%至$6,627億，高於調查預期的4.5%。運輸設備訂單大增21.6%至$1,311億，是整體升幅的主要來源；但出貨也增加1.0%至$6,410億，未交貨訂單上升1.7%至$1.569兆，庫存增加0.3%至$9,591億。

因此，這份報告的改善不只反映單一訂單指標上升，但運輸設備高度集中的貢獻，仍使整體增幅打了折扣。搭配ISM新訂單數據來看，結果顯示部分企業需求依然足以支撐生產與未交貨訂單；但這既未化解就業訊號偏弱，也無法證明面向消費者的經濟活動正以相同速度加速。

市場主要透過實質殖利率反映這項變化。10年期名目殖利率上升5.2個基點之際，實質殖利率升幅更達6.1個基點，損益兩平通膨率則小幅下降。即使油價收高、服務業價格指標仍處高檔，投資人調升的仍是實質政策與成長負擔，而非要求更高的10年期通膨補償。

這並不代表通膨疑慮已經消失，而是顯示眼前的意外在於：既有利率水準之下，經濟仍能維持需求，就業也只是局部轉弱。過去1個月，10年期實質殖利率已上升23.2個基點；同期名目殖利率上升12.5個基點，損益兩平通膨率下降10.7個基點。6月3日的走勢延續了這種由實質利率主導的格局。

殖利率曲線的反應仍相當克制。5年期與10年期券表現落後，30年期殖利率升幅較小，使2s10s陡峭化1.3個基點；2s30s卻未同步變陡，反而平坦化0.3個基點。這種結構使焦點維持在中期政策路徑，並未顯示市場因長期通膨或財政供給而要求大幅提高殖利率補償。

美債現券交易仍相當活絡，但較前一交易日下降。FINRA記錄的面額交易量為$1.113兆，共316,566筆，較6月2日減少5.6%。名目附息債交易量下降9.8%至$8,448億，TIPS交易量下降12.9%至$290億。這些數字呈現本輪重新定價背後的交易規模，卻無法辨識客戶交易方向。

## 聯準會官員對是否需要再次升息意見分歧

面對相同的經濟組合，Logan的解讀比Williams更偏鷹派。她指出，勞動市場大致平衡、AI投資蓬勃，金融環境也保持寬鬆，因此貨幣政策不是中性就是偏鬆，而非具有實質限制性。在這種情況下，她愈來愈擔心今年稍後可能需要升息。

Logan的憂慮不只來自眼前的油價衝擊。她表示，租金與食品價格也已上升，並警告高於目標的通膨若持續太久，可能變得根深蒂固。檢視排除波動項目的衡量方式後，她判斷基礎通膨趨勢正朝2%區間中段發展，而不是一路回到聯準會目標。

她也對一項原可支持較樂觀看法的指標提出保留。聯準會主席Kevin Warsh曾肯定達拉斯聯準銀行的截尾平均通膨指標，但Logan認為，由於技術性因素，該指標目前可能低估通膨。這項警告之所以重要，是因摩根士丹利另一份分析指出，4月12個月截尾平均PCE通膨率為2.35%，遠比聯準會偏好的整體指標3.8%更接近目標。

身為具投票權的委員，Logan已在4月會議上反對暗示下一次利率調整仍較可能是降息的措辭。她6月3日的發言不再只是反對寬鬆傾向，而是進一步主張，至少需要略具限制性的政策才能完成通膨調整；目前的政策設定反而可能仍在支撐需求。

Williams認為兩個方向都沒有迫切調整的必要。他表示，政策目前處於適當位置，近期無須升息或降息，未來動向也沒有明確方向。他承認能源、關稅與AI相關投資帶來上行壓力，但認為服務通膨正在顯著放緩，目前尚未特別擔心出現劇烈的第二輪效應。

Williams的立場部分取決於中東衝突的發展。他表示，若荷莫茲海峽重開，能源價格可能趨穩或下跌。他也認為勞動市場正在穩定，預估2026年經濟成長約2%至2.25%，儘管燃料成本升高會壓抑家庭支出。

褐皮書為辯論雙方都提供了一些依據。聯準會12個地區中有10個的經濟活動以輕微至溫和速度成長，就業大致穩定。受國防活動與資料中心需求支撐，數個地區的製造業聘僱最為強勁；但多數地區仍形容勞動市場處於「低聘僱、低裁員」狀態，招募集中在關鍵職位與人員替補需求。

價格壓力則更為普遍。各地聯絡人將中東衝突引發的能源成本列為主要通膨來源，且影響已擴及運輸、包裝、食品雜貨與肥料。紐約地區一家食品生產商表示，能源成本正在推高包裝、原料、設備及零件支出，肥料價格上漲也帶動食品成本。在費城，部分員工因燃料支出增加而要求加薪。

不過，企業也擔心客戶抗拒漲價。聖路易一家旅宿業者選擇減少服務，而非提高價格；數個地區並回報消費支出轉弱，燃料成本的不確定性升高。未來6個月的成長展望幾乎未變。這些證據顯示能源成本已實際傳導至企業端，卻不足以證明企業能將每一項增幅全數轉嫁至終端價格或工資。

美國財政部長Scott Bessent則提出政府較為樂觀的解讀，稱本輪通膨升高只是短期干擾，並主張衝突結束後能源價格便會回落。他也重申，要在總統Donald Trump卸任前將聯邦預算赤字降至GDP的4%以下。不過，報導所引述的多數經濟學家預期，隨國防與利息成本增加，今年赤字將擴大至6%以上；因此，財政目標與眼前的貨幣政策爭議仍是兩項不同議題。

聯準會監理報告另對信用情勢提出較窄範圍的保留。2025年期間，數類銀行貸款的逾期率小幅上升，但聯準會表示，多數機構資本充足，銀行體系依然穩健。下半年消費貸款逾期率溫和增加；數起引人注目的非銀行機構違約，也使市場更關注私募信貸，並促使部分銀行重新檢視相關曝險的擔保品作法。

因此，6月會議開場時的分歧不只在於通膨問題有多嚴重，也包括目前政策究竟具有多大限制性。Logan認為，需求展現韌性、金融環境寬鬆，足以成為考慮再次升息的理由；Williams則主張可以等待能源衝擊、服務通膨與勞動市場進一步演變。服務業調查的就業分項與褐皮書所呈現的客戶抗拒漲價，也使鷹派論點不能簡化為經濟再次過熱。

## 美國財政部操作吸收短端與長端供給

美國財政部標售$690億、119天期國庫券，最高貼現率為3.635%，投資收益率為3.730%。投標倍數達3.15倍，其中93.35%按最高利率獲配。獲接受的競爭性投標共$683.8億，另有$5.22億非競爭性投標，以及外國官方機構投標的$1億。

該券將於6月9日交割、10月6日到期。由於沒有發行前交易水準可供比較，結果只能確認正式標售利率與需求倍數，無法判斷得標利率優於或落後當時市價。儘管附息債殖利率上升，本次標售沒有顯示融資壓力。

殖利率曲線另一端，財政部在預定的流動性支持買回操作中，足額接受上限$20億的20年至30年期名目附息債。交易商在本次操作合計報售$212.6億債券；36檔合格債券中，財政部接受其中14檔的報價，並將於6月4日交割。

報售規模遠高於買回上限，顯示市場有相當意願把非指標長天期債券售回財政部；不過，這項操作旨在支持流動性，並非因應市場失序。合格債券的到期日介於2046年8月至2056年5月。當天30年期殖利率上升3.6個基點，升幅小於10年期券；買回操作則吸收了一小部分長天期債券供給。

下一階段供給將從6月4日的公告展開，內容涵蓋次週的3年期公債、增額發行的10年期與30年期公債，以及6月8日標售的13週與26週國庫券。5月再融資政策顯示附息債發行規模不變，但正式金額與交割條件仍須等待公告確認。

財政部另將於6月4日美東時間13:40至14:00進行現金管理買回，最高買回$125億、期限介於1個月至2年的名目附息債，並於6月5日交割。這項交易不同於長端流動性操作，會直接影響近期現金管理與短天期附息債供給。

## 亞洲與歐洲面對不同的成長與通膨組合

美國以外最新且最明確的緊縮信號來自日本央行總裁植田和男。他表示，若物價上行風險超過中東危機對經濟活動可能造成的損害，政策委員會便需要討論升息。根據目前資料與企業回報，他判斷通膨風險較大，而且可能比成長下行風險更早出現。

這番話明確將6月升息納入考量，但尚未使其成為定局。交易員估計，6月15日至16日會議升息25個基點的機率約為85%，若成真，政策利率將升至1995年以來最高。政策委員會4月以6票對3票決定按兵不動，為植田任內分歧最大的一次表決；當時支持維持政策的兩名委員後來也贊成近期升息，但未指明特定會議。

油價與日圓走勢進一步強化升息理由。儘管日本在4月28日至5月27日間投入創紀錄的¥11.73兆干預匯市，日圓6月3日仍一度觸及160兌1美元，並在植田發言後交投於159.83附近。財務大臣片山皋月重申，政府已準備因應匯率變動，但拒絕說明特定價位。

日本內閣另通過¥3.1兆追加預算，以減輕衝突相關通膨對家庭的衝擊，其中包括¥2.5兆準備金，初期預計用於汽油補貼。支出將透過赤字融資公債籌措，但政府計畫取消原訂截至6月的其他發債，使按日程計算的市場總供給維持不變。

植田表示，即使升息，金融環境仍會保持寬鬆，並認為經濟有能力承受這項衝擊。東京通膨雖已降至4年低點，資本支出也弱於預期，但他強調油價未來可能推高物價，以及日本央行對截至明年3月年度所作的2.8%通膨預測。政策委員會將另行決定，下一會計年度是否繼續每季減少¥2,000億購債。

澳洲則出現較為分歧的政策訊號。第1季GDP成長0.3%，僅為第4季增速的三分之一，也低於預期。以資料中心為主的民間投資增加近4%；機械與設備支出大增16%，為近30年最大升幅。西太平洋銀行估計，資料中心投資及其外溢效應貢獻了當季全部經濟成長。

家庭支出轉弱、淨出口下降、生產力放緩，單位勞動成本卻仍處高檔。因此，在3次升息與能源衝擊的完整影響尚未浮現前，經濟動能便已減弱；但GDP的組成也未向澳洲央行提供國內成本壓力正在消退的明確證據。

數據公布後，澳洲3年期公債殖利率下降。市場預期澳洲央行6月中旬將把現金利率維持在4.35%，認為8月再度升息的機率約各半，並已完全反映12月前升息一次。A$10億的2033年11月到期澳洲公債標售，需求超過發行額4倍，投標倍數創7年期券自11月標售以來最高。

中國服務業則提供較強的區域成長訊號。RatingDog服務業PMI由4月的52.6升至5月的54.4，綜合產出指數也由53.1升至54.0。新業務加速，出口訂單恢復成長，就業則為4個月來首次增加。投入成本通膨升至19個月高點，但銷售價格大致不變，顯示企業尚未將成本完全轉嫁給客戶。

歐元區面對的組合正好相反：經濟活動萎縮，價格壓力卻轉強。綜合PMI終值由48.8降至48.5，但已從47.5的初值向上修正。服務業指數由47.6微升至47.7，也高於46.4的初值，卻仍處萎縮區間。新訂單下降、就業流失加快，投入與產出價格通膨均升高。

官方生產者價格數據進一步強化上游通膨疑慮。歐元區4月工業產品價格較前月上升0.6%、較去年同期上升4.9%。排除能源後，價格月增0.9%、年增2.3%，中間財價格則大增1.8%。能源價格下降0.4%，顯示整體月增幅並非單純由能源造成。

波蘭則顯示，國內通膨放緩仍可能中斷全球升息趨勢。5月通膨意外下降後，央行總裁Adam Glapinski表示，3.75%的政策利率已足夠高，沒有理由討論調整。自伊朗戰爭爆發以來，市場一度反映最多74個基點的升息；這番談話為預期降溫後，3x6遠期利率協議較3個月Wibor高出38個基點。

OECD也對市場所預期的英國央行利率路徑提出不同看法。儘管預估英國今年與明年平均通膨率分別為3.7%與2.4%，OECD仍預測英國央行將在2026年維持利率不變，至2027年才降息25個基點至3.5%。市場則預期9月前升息25個基點。OECD認為能源衝擊只是暫時現象，較弱的勞動市場將限制第二輪壓力；同時建議持續縮減資產負債表，財政支援則應採取針對性措施，而非廣泛補貼。

新興市場對通膨的反應普遍更快。自伊朗衝突爆發以來，至少已有10家新興與前緣市場央行升息；過去兩週採取緊縮行動的包括印尼、盧安達、南非與斯里蘭卡。除了油價、液化天然氣、肥料與食品價格上漲直接推升通膨外，捍衛匯率與防範資本外流也強化了升息壓力。

印度反映了這些壓力如何同時改變主權債定價與企業融資。截至5月15日止1年，銀行信用成長16.2%，為2024年6月以來最快；國內債券發行量則下降11%至10.9兆盧比。衝突爆發以來，政府公債殖利率已上升38個基點至7.04%，使部分評級較低企業的銀行貸款成本比發債低60至70個基點。

信用成長已連續第8個月高於存款成長，差距並擴大至約400個基點。銀行因此更仰賴可轉讓定期存單融資，推動6個月期CD利率在5月上升88個基點，創4年最大單月升幅。企業目前可藉此降低借款成本，資金壓力卻轉移至銀行資產負債表，時間點正值印度央行6月5日決策前夕。

## 信用供給管道擴大，主權債談判出現進展

AI相關借款持續在信用市場擴張，投資人也開始爭論，融資規模最終是否會超過可支應債務的現金流。自2025年初以來，美國投資級債、高收益債、貸款及其他AI相關融資的發行規模已超過$3,700億。彭博行業研究估計，未來5年AI資本支出可能接近$5兆，其中很大一部分將透過舉債融資。

摩根士丹利的Anish Shah估計，AI在2026年可能占全部信用發行量的10%至15%，相較之下，兩年前幾乎沒有占比。該行預期，今年美國投資級債銷售將創下$2.25兆紀錄，其中超大規模雲端業者的發行額將達$2,500億至$3,000億。

DoubleLine投資組合經理Robert Cohen認為，這類投資熱潮最終會形成泡沫條件，但他與其他與談人也表示，信用市場目前尚未走到那一步。個別交易若有獲利良好的科技公司支撐、具備合約現金流並採分期攤還結構，風險可望降低。他擔心的是，投資人接受的利差已假設借款人未來能成長到足以履行債務。

Alphabet計畫進入市政預付能源融資，顯示資金管道已擴展到新的領域。Alphabet被列為California Community Choice Financing Authority一筆$10億交易的資金接收方，該交易將為Pioneer Community Energy提供長期折價電力供應，債券預計取得穆迪Aa2評級。

Alphabet將成為已知首家在這類市政融資架構中擔任資金接收方的美國科技公司。這項角色可讓資金接收方使用免稅融資，並將募集款項按應稅利率投資，同時透過付款協助公用事業取得能源。投資人獲得的殖利率通常也高於評級相近的傳統市政債。

這項架構為資料中心相關能源需求提供了另一條融資管道；但若超大規模雲端業者廣泛採用，也會引發市政債市場容量是否足夠的疑問。為支應不斷增加的AI投資，Alphabet另將本週宣布的一套股權融資方案提高至接近$850億。

環境規範則帶來另一種公司債資金流向。管理資產逾$2,700億的瑞士機構投資人計畫在現有持債到期後，停止買進Chevron、Exxon Mobil、Marathon Petroleum、PBF Energy、Phillips 66、Valero Energy與Saudi Aramco發行的債券。瑞士責任投資協會此前與相關公司溝通，但減排進展不足，因而提出排除建議。

這項建議適用於債券而非股票；對於股票部位，會員仍被建議繼續行使投票權。該協會代表的機構合計管理3,600億瑞士法郎資產，但部分會員仍在評估指引。此項變化使上述發行人明確失去一部分需求，卻不足以證明整體能源業信用債已重新定價。

主權債方面，尚比亞開始朝與債權人磋商的方向發展；這些持有人先前阻止政府回購一檔$13.6億、2053年到期債券。知情人士表示，控制該券逾25%的債權人團體可能簽署保密協議並展開非公開談判；另一名人士則稱協商尚未開始，因此時程與結果都未確定。

這批債權人持有足以阻擋交易的部位，使尚比亞無法運用清理贖回權，贖回收購要約完成後的剩餘債券。該券價格接近每1美元面額81美分，高於政府提出的78美分，使持有人缺乏參與誘因。這項爭議之所以重要，是因若尚比亞連續兩期通過IMF債務可持續性測試，票息可能由0.5%升至7.5%；兩次測試預計分別在6月與12月進行。

阿根廷則達成較有利的外匯存底里程碑。央行6月3日買進$4,300萬，使去年12月設定目標以來的美元累計購買額突破$100億。農作物產量創紀錄、能源出口成長92%，以及省級政府與企業增加海外借款，都為美元流入提供支撐。

這些購匯已協助政府在不重返國際市場的情況下履行債務義務，主權債利差也收窄至Javier Milei擔任總統以來的低點附近。不過，美元同時因償債流出，改善仍不完整。即使外匯存底總額略高於$480億，按市價計算的淨存底僅約$30億；阿根廷在最近一次$200億IMF計畫審查中，也未達成淨存底目標。

隨2027年債務付款將超過$300億，總購匯額與可用淨存底之間的差異會更加重要。購匯里程碑降低了市場對短期美元取得能力的擔憂，但可用淨存底增幅有限，使主權信用仍易受持續外部融資需求與選舉壓力影響。

## 後續市場意義

修正後的美國第1季生產力與單位勞動成本將於6月4日美東時間08:30公布。初值顯示生產力按年率成長0.8%，單位勞動成本上升2.3%。修正結果將決定近期工資成長是由產出增加所支撐，還是更直接地加重通膨壓力。

首次申請失業救濟人數將於同一時間公布；截至5月23日當週的初報數字為21.5萬人。這是非農就業前最後一項高頻勞動市場檢驗。在ADP增幅較強、服務業調查就業分項處於萎縮，以及褐皮書呈現低聘僱、低裁員狀態之後，本次數據尤其重要。

6月5日公布的5月就業報告，仍是檢驗本輪美債重新定價的主要數據。市場預期非農就業增加9.3萬人，前值為11.5萬人；失業率前值為4.3%，平均時薪則月增0.2%、年增3.6%。聘僱廣度、失業率、工時與工資將共同決定，服務業就業指標偏弱的影響是否足以超過ADP與職缺數據所顯示的趨穩跡象。

印度央行也將在3天會議結束後於6月5日公布政策決定。目前附買回利率為5.25%，政策立場中性。決策須在進口能源通膨、盧比與資金壓力、企業融資由債券轉向銀行貸款，以及進一步緊縮對成長造成的代價之間取得平衡。

6月8日，紐約聯準銀行消費者調查將更新家庭通膨預期。4月數據分別為1年期3.6%、3年期3.1%、5年期3.0%。結果將直接檢驗Logan對通膨長期高於目標、可能變得根深蒂固的憂慮，也能衡量Williams認為第二輪效應可望受到控制的看法。

美債供給隨後將由公告進入實際操作。3年期公債預定6月9日標售；在發行規模不變的政策下，預計金額為$580億，同日下午10年至20年期流動性支持買回最多可接受$20億。增額發行的10年期公債將於6月10日標售，正式條件公布後，預計規模為$390億。

5月CPI同樣將於6月10日美東時間08:30公布，是6月16日至17日FOMC會議前最關鍵的通膨數據。4月整體通膨月增0.6%、年增3.8%，核心通膨月增0.4%、年增2.8%。能源、住宅與其他核心服務之間的分布，將決定6月3日實質殖利率上升主要仍是經濟活動與政策路徑的調整，或將進一步演變為通膨補償普遍走高。

overall_summary.headline: 服務業需求與油價維持升息風險，實質殖利率帶動美債走跌
overall_summary.session_narrative:
美國服務業需求轉強、民間聘僱展現韌性，加上油價再度上漲，使聯準會仍有進一步升息的可能，美債於6月3日全面走跌。2年期殖利率上升3.9個基點至4.083%，5年期上升4.7個基點至4.217%，10年期上升5.2個基點至4.496%，30年期則上升3.6個基點至4.993%。

本輪調整由實質利率主導，而非長期通膨補償上升：10年期實質殖利率增加6.1個基點至2.104%，10年期損益兩平通膨率反而下降0.9個基點至2.392%。ADP公布民間就業增加12.2萬人；ISM服務業指數也因商業活動與新訂單轉強而升至54.5。不過，ISM就業分項仍處萎縮區間，較疲弱的標普全球調查更顯示，服務業就業流失速度為2020年5月以來最快。油價上漲與服務業價格指標處於高檔，使需求韌性仍足以影響政策前景。

Lorie Logan表示，由於通膨似乎正朝2%區間中段發展，金融環境也維持寬鬆，2026年稍後可能需要升息。John Williams則認為政策校準適當，近期沒有向任一方向調整的必要。美國以外，植田和男認為通膨風險比成長受損更為迫切，將日本央行6月升息明確納入考量。收盤結果顯示升息疑慮仍在，卻未出現全面避險；接下來美國非農就業與CPI將決定，就業疲弱的證據能否壓過需求堅挺與價格壓力持續的影響。
overall_summary.summary: 服務業走強、民間聘僱展現韌性，加上油價再次上漲，推動10年期美債殖利率上升5.2個基點至4.496%；但就業分項仍在萎縮、聯準會官員意見分歧，非農就業與通膨因而成為後續關鍵檢驗。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Treasuries sold off on June 3 as stronger U.S. services demand, resilient private hiring and another rise in oil prices preserved the possibility of Federal Reserve tightening. The 10-year yield rose 5.2 basis points to 4.496%, its largest increase in two weeks, while the 5-year added 4.7 basis points to 4.217%. The 2-year yield increased 3.9 basis points to 4.083%, and the 30-year rose 3.6 basis points to 4.993%.

The modest steepening from 2 to 10 years reflected a repricing led by real rates rather than higher long-term inflation compensation. The 10-year real yield climbed 6.1 basis points to 2.104%, while the 10-year breakeven fell 0.9 basis point to 2.392%. The 2s10s curve widened 1.3 basis points to 41.3 basis points, but 2s30s was almost unchanged at 91 basis points as the long bond outperformed the 10-year sector.

May data gave investors evidence of continuing demand without resolving weakness beneath the labor-market headline. ADP reported 122,000 private-sector jobs, slightly more than economists expected. The ISM services index then rose to 54.5 from 53.6, beating a 53.7 survey estimate as business activity and new orders accelerated. Yet employment remained in contraction at 47.9, while a separate S&P Global survey showed only marginal services growth and the fastest job shedding since May 2020.

Inflation details kept the stronger activity data consequential for rates. ISM’s prices index increased to 71.3 from 70.7, and the Federal Reserve’s Beige Book found energy costs spreading into shipping, packaging, groceries and fertilizer across much of the country. WTI crude rose 2.41% to $96.02 and Brent gained 1.89% to $97.81, reversing part of the recent relief associated with expectations for a settlement in the Middle East.

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan, an FOMC voter who dissented against the April statement’s easing bias, supplied the clearest policy response. She said rates may need to rise later in 2026 because inflation appears to be trending toward the mid-2% range rather than returning to 2%, while the labor market is broadly balanced and financial conditions remain accommodative. New York Fed President John Williams took a less directional position, judging current policy appropriately calibrated and seeing no immediate need to move either way.

The result was a broad but orderly increase in Treasury yields rather than a renewed rise in inflation compensation or a generalized flight from risk. The S&P 500 fell 0.74%, the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.29% and the VIX rose 1.84% to 16.06, while the semiconductor index gained 1.39%. The dollar strengthened 0.31%, gold fell 1.17%, and listed investment-grade, high-yield and emerging-market debt funds lost between 0.22% and 0.37%. The session left the market’s tightening concern intact, but the divergence between robust services demand and contracting employment made the coming official payroll and inflation reports more important than the headline strength alone.

## Services Demand Lifts Real Yields

The Treasury selloff began before the U.S. releases as oil recovered and the outlook for a rapid settlement of the Iran conflict became less certain. Yields extended their rise after ADP estimated that private employers added 122,000 jobs in May, providing another indication that labor demand had stabilized after April job openings exceeded expectations.

The ADP result did not establish broad acceleration in employment, but it reduced the likelihood that an abrupt labor-market break would force the Fed to look through elevated inflation. TD Securities rates strategist Molly Brooks said the reading reinforced signs of stabilization. In her assessment, even subpar official payroll growth might not generate a large market response unless the weakness was substantial enough to redirect attention away from inflation.

The ISM services report strengthened the demand side of that argument. Its headline index increased 0.9 point to 54.5, above the 53.7 survey estimate. Business activity rose to 57.7 from 55.9, and new orders accelerated to 57.3 from 53.5. The increases showed that the expansion was not merely the result of slower supplier deliveries or inventory accumulation.

Inventories nevertheless made an unusually large contribution. The index jumped to 62.5 from 53.1, matching its record, while supplier deliveries eased to 55.2 from 56.8. That composition suggests some businesses were building stock against uncertain supply conditions even as final activity remained firm. It adds resilience to current output but leaves open whether all of the accumulation will be sustained if household demand weakens.

The employment component supplied an important counter-signal, slipping to 47.9 from 48.0 and remaining below the 50 threshold. The report therefore combined stronger orders and activity with continued contraction in service-sector employment. That split matters for the Fed because it allows officials to see current demand as resilient without concluding that hiring is reaccelerating across the economy.

S&P Global’s final services survey was softer still. Its business-activity index declined to 50.7 from 51.0, slightly below the 50.9 flash estimate and consistent with only marginal growth. Employment fell at the fastest pace since May 2020, business optimism dropped to its lowest since October 2022 and foreign demand posted its sharpest decline since November 2022. New business returned to growth, but the survey did not show the same breadth of expansion as ISM.

The two services surveys consequently altered the assessment in different ways rather than providing duplicate confirmation. ISM showed faster domestic activity and orders, while both surveys indicated weak employment. S&P also found input-cost inflation at a five-month high, and ISM’s prices index rose to 71.3. The common signal was that softer hiring had not yet produced a clean reduction in business cost pressure.

April factory orders added a stronger hard-data reading. Orders rose 4.8% to $662.7 billion after a revised 1.8% March increase, exceeding the 4.5% survey expectation. Transportation-equipment orders climbed 21.6% to $131.1 billion and drove much of the headline gain, but shipments also increased 1.0% to $641 billion, unfilled orders rose 1.7% to $1.569 trillion and inventories advanced 0.3% to $959.1 billion.

The release was therefore broader than a single increase in bookings, although the concentration in transportation equipment qualified the scale of the headline. Together with the ISM new-orders reading, it showed that parts of business demand remained firm enough to sustain production and backlogs. It did not resolve the weaker employment indications or establish that consumer-facing activity was accelerating at the same pace.

Market pricing located the adjustment mainly in real yields. The 10-year nominal yield’s 5.2-basis-point rise was accompanied by a 6.1-basis-point increase in the real yield and a small decline in breakeven inflation. Investors marked up the real policy and growth burden rather than requiring more 10-year inflation compensation, despite the higher oil close and elevated services-price measures.

That distinction does not mean inflation concern disappeared. It shows that the immediate surprise was the economy’s ability to sustain demand under existing rates while employment weakened only unevenly. Over the previous month, the 10-year real yield had risen 23.2 basis points, compared with a 12.5-basis-point increase in the nominal yield and a 10.7-basis-point decline in the breakeven. June 3 extended that real-rate-led pattern.

The curve response was restrained. The 5- and 10-year sectors underperformed, while the 30-year yield rose less. The resulting 1.3-basis-point steepening in 2s10s did not carry into 2s30s, which flattened 0.3 basis point. That configuration kept the focus on the medium-term policy path rather than indicating a large new concession for long-run inflation or fiscal supply.

Treasury cash activity remained substantial but declined from the previous session. FINRA recorded $1.113 trillion of par trading across 316,566 transactions, 5.6% less than on June 2. Nominal-coupon activity fell 9.8% to $844.8 billion, while TIPS activity declined 12.9% to $29 billion. The figures establish the volume behind the repricing without identifying the direction of customer transactions.

## Fed Officials Split Over the Need for Another Increase

Logan interpreted the same economic configuration more hawkishly than Williams. She said the labor market was broadly balanced, AI investment was booming and financial conditions were accommodative, leaving monetary policy either neutral or loose rather than meaningfully restrictive. In that setting, she was increasingly concerned that a rate increase could be required later this year.

Her concern extended beyond the immediate oil shock. Logan said rent and food prices had also increased and warned that above-target inflation could become entrenched if it persisted. After examining measures that remove volatile components, she judged the underlying trend to be moving toward the mid-2% range, not all the way back to the Fed’s objective.

Logan also qualified one measure that could otherwise support a more benign interpretation. She said the Dallas Fed trimmed-mean inflation gauge, which Chairman Kevin Warsh has praised, was probably understating current inflation because of a technical factor. That warning matters because a separate Morgan Stanley analysis noted that the 12-month trimmed-mean PCE rate was 2.35% in April, substantially closer to target than the 3.8% increase in the Fed’s headline preferred measure.

As a voting member, Logan had already dissented at the April meeting over language indicating that the next rate move remained more likely to be a cut. Her June 3 remarks moved beyond opposition to an easing bias: she argued that at least mildly restrictive policy was needed to complete the inflation adjustment and that the current setting might instead be supporting demand.

Williams saw less urgency in either direction. He said policy was in the right place and that he saw no immediate need to raise or lower rates, nor an obvious direction for future moves. He acknowledged upward pressure from energy, tariffs and AI-related investment, but said services inflation was slowing substantially and that he was not yet especially worried about dramatic second-round effects.

His position depended partly on the path of the Middle East conflict. Williams said energy prices could stabilize or fall if the Strait of Hormuz reopened. He also judged the labor market to be stabilizing and expected economic growth of about 2% to 2.25% in 2026, even as higher fuel costs weighed on household spending.

The Beige Book gave each side of that debate some support. Economic activity increased at a slight to moderate pace in 10 of the Fed’s 12 districts, and employment was broadly stable. Manufacturing hiring was strongest in several districts, supported by defense activity and data-center demand, while most regions continued to describe a low-hire, low-fire labor market in which recruitment focused on critical roles and replacement needs.

Price pressure was more widespread. District contacts identified energy costs associated with the Middle East conflict as the principal inflation driver, with spillovers into shipping, packaging, groceries and fertilizer. A New York-area food producer reported that energy was raising the cost of packaging, ingredients, equipment and parts, while higher fertilizer prices were lifting food costs. In Philadelphia, some employees sought wage increases because of higher fuel expenses.

Businesses nevertheless expressed concern about customer resistance. A St. Louis hospitality company reduced services rather than raise prices, and several districts reported weakening consumer spending and uncertainty about fuel costs. The six-month outlook showed little change in expected growth. That evidence describes active pass-through into business costs without proving that companies can transmit every increase into final prices or wages.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent presented the administration’s more benign interpretation, calling the inflation rise a short-term disturbance and arguing that energy prices would retreat when the conflict ended. He also reiterated an objective of reducing the federal budget deficit below 4% of GDP before President Donald Trump leaves office. Most economists cited in the account expected the deficit to widen above 6% this year as defense and interest costs increased, leaving the fiscal goal separate from the immediate monetary-policy dispute.

The Fed’s supervisory report added a narrower credit qualification. Bank-loan delinquency rates increased modestly across several categories during 2025, although the central bank said most institutions were well capitalized and the banking system remained strong. Consumer-loan delinquencies increased moderately in the second half, while several prominent nonbank defaults prompted closer attention to private credit and led some banks to revisit collateral practices for related exposures.

The June meeting will therefore begin with disagreement not only over the size of the inflation problem but over how restrictive current policy is. Logan sees resilient demand and accommodative conditions as reasons to contemplate another increase. Williams sees scope to wait for the energy shock and services inflation to evolve. The employment components of the services surveys and the Beige Book’s customer-resistance evidence prevent the hawkish case from becoming a simple claim of renewed overheating.

## Treasury Operations Absorb Front- and Long-End Supply

Treasury’s $69 billion 119-day bill auction produced a 3.635% high discount rate and a 3.730% investment rate. The sale attracted a 3.15 bid-to-cover ratio, with 93.35% allotted at the high rate. Accepted competitive tenders totaled $68.380 billion, alongside $522 million of noncompetitive bids and $100 million from foreign official institutions.

The bill settles June 9 and matures October 6. Without a supplied when-issued reference, the result establishes the official cash rate and demand ratio but does not show whether bidding cleared through or behind prevailing market levels. It offered no indication of funding stress as coupon yields rose.

At the other end of the curve, Treasury accepted the full $2 billion maximum in its scheduled liquidity-support buyback of 20- to 30-year nominal coupons. Dealers offered $21.26 billion across the operation, and Treasury accepted securities from 14 of the 36 eligible issues. Settlement is June 4.

The large amount offered relative to the maximum showed substantial willingness to sell off-the-run long debt back to Treasury, but the operation was designed to support liquidity rather than respond to market disorder. Its eligible maturities ran from August 2046 through May 2056. The buyback absorbed a small amount of long-duration supply during a session in which the 30-year yield rose 3.6 basis points, less than the increase in the 10-year sector.

The next phase of supply begins with June 4 announcements covering the following week’s 3-year note, reopened 10-year and 30-year securities, and June 8 sales of 13- and 26-week bills. The May refunding policy indicated unchanged coupon sizes, but the formal amounts and settlement terms remain subject to those announcements.

Treasury will also conduct a cash-management buyback of as much as $12.5 billion in 1-month to 2-year nominal coupons from 13:40 to 14:00 ET on June 4, settling June 5. Unlike the long-end liquidity operation, that transaction directly changes near-term cash management and the supply of short-dated coupons.

## Asia and Europe Confront Different Growth-Inflation Mixes

Bank of Japan Governor Kazuo Ueda gave the clearest new tightening signal outside the U.S. He said the board would need to discuss raising rates if upside risks to prices outweighed the potential damage to activity from the Middle East crisis. Based on the available data and business reports, he judged inflation risks to be larger and likely to emerge sooner than the downside risks to growth.

The remarks placed a June increase firmly under consideration without making it certain. Traders assigned roughly an 85% probability to a quarter-point move at the June 15-16 meeting, which would lift the benchmark to its highest level since 1995. The board had held policy in April by a 6-3 vote, its largest split under Ueda, and two members who supported that hold subsequently endorsed a near-term increase without specifying the meeting.

Oil and the yen reinforced the case. The currency touched 160 per dollar on June 3 and traded near 159.83 after Ueda’s remarks, despite Japan’s record ¥11.73 trillion of intervention between April 28 and May 27. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reiterated that the government was ready to respond to foreign-exchange moves, while declining to identify a specific level.

Japan’s cabinet also approved a ¥3.1 trillion supplementary budget to cushion households from conflict-related inflation, including a ¥2.5 trillion reserve expected initially to support gasoline subsidies. The spending will use deficit-financing bonds, but the government plans to cancel other issuance scheduled through June so that total market supply is unchanged on a calendar basis.

Ueda said financial conditions would remain accommodative even after an increase and maintained that the economy could withstand the shock. Tokyo inflation had slowed to a four-year low and capital spending was weaker than expected, but he emphasized the prospective lift from oil and the BOJ’s 2.8% inflation forecast for the year ending in March. The board will separately decide whether to continue reducing bond purchases by ¥200 billion per quarter in the next fiscal year.

Australia delivered a more divided policy signal. First-quarter GDP increased 0.3%, only one-third of the fourth quarter’s pace and below estimates. Private investment rose almost 4%, led by data centers, and machinery-and-equipment spending jumped 16%, its largest increase in nearly 30 years. Westpac estimated that data-center investment and its spillovers accounted for all of the quarter’s growth.

Household spending weakened, net exports declined and productivity slowed, while unit labor costs remained elevated. The economy was therefore losing momentum before the full effects of three rate increases and the energy shock arrived, but the composition did not give the Reserve Bank of Australia clear evidence that domestic cost pressure was subsiding.

Three-year Australian yields fell after the release. Markets expected the RBA to hold its 4.35% cash rate in mid-June, assigned roughly even odds to another increase in August and fully priced a move by December. Demand at a A$1 billion auction of November 2033 government bonds exceeded four times the amount offered, the strongest bid-to-cover ratio for a 7-year sale since that maturity was auctioned in November.

China’s services economy offered a firmer regional growth signal. The RatingDog services PMI rose to 54.4 in May from 52.6, and the composite output index increased to 54.0 from 53.1. New business accelerated, export orders returned to growth and employment increased for the first time in four months. Input-cost inflation reached a 19-month high, although selling prices were broadly unchanged, indicating that businesses had not fully passed those costs to customers.

The euro area faced the opposite combination of contracting activity and stronger prices. The final composite PMI fell to 48.5 from 48.8, although it was revised above the 47.5 flash estimate. Services edged up to 47.7 from 47.6 and were also stronger than the 46.4 flash reading, but remained in contraction. New orders declined, job losses accelerated and both input- and output-price inflation strengthened.

Official producer-price data reinforced the pipeline inflation concern. Euro-area industrial prices rose 0.6% in April and 4.9% from a year earlier. Excluding energy, prices gained 0.9% on the month and 2.3% over the year, while intermediate-goods prices jumped 1.8%. Energy prices fell 0.4%, showing that the monthly increase was not simply an energy effect.

Poland demonstrated that softer domestic inflation could still interrupt the global tightening trend. Central-bank Governor Adam Glapinski said the 3.75% policy rate was high enough and that there was no reason to discuss a change after May inflation unexpectedly declined. The statement cooled a market that had priced as much as 74 basis points of tightening since the Iran war began; 3x6 forward-rate agreements subsequently traded 38 basis points above 3-month Wibor.

The OECD also challenged the market’s expected path for the Bank of England. It forecast that the BOE would keep rates unchanged during 2026 and cut them by 25 basis points to 3.5% in 2027, even as UK inflation averages 3.7% this year and 2.4% next year. Markets instead expected a quarter-point increase by September. The OECD viewed the energy shock as temporary and the weaker labor market as a constraint on second-round pressure, while urging continued balance-sheet reduction and targeted rather than broad fiscal support.

Across emerging markets, the inflation response has generally been faster. At least 10 emerging and frontier central banks have raised rates since the Iran conflict began, with Indonesia, Rwanda, South Africa and Sri Lanka tightening during the previous two weeks. Currency defense and concern about capital outflows have reinforced the direct inflation response to higher oil, liquefied natural gas, fertilizer and food prices.

India illustrates how those pressures are changing both sovereign pricing and corporate finance. Bank credit grew 16.2% in the year through May 15, the fastest since June 2024, while domestic bond issuance fell 11% to 10.9 trillion rupees. Government yields had risen 38 basis points to 7.04% since the conflict began, making bank loans 60 to 70 basis points cheaper than bonds for some lower-rated companies.

Credit growth exceeded deposit growth for an eighth consecutive month, and the gap widened to about 400 basis points. Banks consequently turned more heavily to certificates of deposit, pushing 6-month CD rates 88 basis points higher in May, the largest monthly increase in four years. The shift lowers borrowing costs for companies now but transfers funding pressure to bank balance sheets ahead of the Reserve Bank of India’s June 5 decision.

## Credit Supply Broadens as Sovereign Negotiations Advance

AI-related borrowing continued to expand across credit markets, even as investors debated whether the volume would eventually exceed the cash flows available to support it. More than $370 billion of U.S. high-grade bonds, junk debt, loans and other AI-linked financing had been issued since the start of 2025. Bloomberg Intelligence estimated AI capital expenditure could approach $5 trillion over the next five years, much of it financed through debt.

Morgan Stanley’s Anish Shah estimated that AI could account for 10% to 15% of all credit issuance in 2026, compared with almost no presence two years earlier. The bank expects a record $2.25 trillion of U.S. high-grade bond sales this year, including $250 billion to $300 billion from hyperscalers.

DoubleLine portfolio manager Robert Cohen argued that such investment booms eventually produce bubble conditions, although he and other panelists said the credit market had not reached that point. Support from profitable technology companies, contractual cash flows and amortizing structures can reduce risk in individual transactions. His concern centered on buying debt at spreads that assume borrowers will grow into their obligations.

Alphabet’s planned entrance into municipal prepaid-energy financing showed how far the funding channels are broadening. The company was identified as the funding recipient for a $1 billion California Community Choice Financing Authority transaction supporting a long-term discounted electricity supply for Pioneer Community Energy. The bonds are expected to carry a Moody’s rating of Aa2.

Alphabet would be the first known U.S. technology company to serve as the funding recipient in such a municipal structure. The role allows the recipient to access tax-exempt financing and invest proceeds at taxable rates while making payments that help procure energy for the utility. Investors generally receive more yield than on conventional municipal bonds with similar ratings.

The structure provides another route for financing energy demand associated with data centers, but it also raises questions about the municipal market’s capacity if hyperscalers use it extensively. Alphabet separately increased a package of equity financing announced during the week to almost $85 billion as it funds growing AI investment.

Environmental mandates created a different corporate-bond flow. Swiss institutional investors managing more than $270 billion plan to stop buying bonds issued by Chevron, Exxon Mobil, Marathon Petroleum, PBF Energy, Phillips 66, Valero Energy and Saudi Aramco as existing holdings mature. The decision followed an exclusion recommendation from the Swiss Association for Responsible Investments after engagement failed to produce sufficient progress on emissions.

The recommendation applies to debt rather than equities, where members were advised to continue exercising voting rights. The association represents institutions with 360 billion Swiss francs of combined assets, although some members were still considering the guidance. The change creates an identifiable loss of demand for the named issuers without establishing a broader repricing of energy-sector credit.

In sovereign debt, Zambia moved toward discussions with holders who blocked its effort to repurchase a $1.36 billion 2053 bond. A creditor group controlling more than 25% of the issue could sign non-disclosure agreements and enter confidential talks, according to people familiar with the matter. Another person said negotiations had not yet begun, leaving both the timing and outcome unresolved.

The blocking position prevents Zambia from using a clean-up call to redeem bonds left after the tender. The securities traded near 81 cents on the dollar, above the government’s 78-cent offer, reducing the incentive to participate. The dispute matters because the coupon could rise to 7.5% from 0.5% if Zambia satisfies an IMF debt-sustainability test for two consecutive periods, expected first in June and again in December.

Argentina reached a more favorable reserve milestone. The central bank bought $43 million on June 3, pushing its cumulative dollar purchases above the $10 billion target set in December. Record crop volumes, a 92% increase in energy exports and increased foreign borrowing by provinces and companies supported the inflow.

The purchases have helped the government meet debt obligations without returning to international markets, and sovereign spreads narrowed near their lowest levels under President Javier Milei. The improvement remains incomplete because dollars have also flowed out for debt service. Net reserves were around $3 billion at market prices, despite gross reserves slightly above $48 billion, and Argentina missed the net-reserve target in the latest review of its $20 billion IMF program.

That distinction becomes more important as debt payments rise above $30 billion in 2027. The gross-purchase milestone reduces immediate concern about access to dollars, while the limited increase in usable net reserves leaves the sovereign exposed to continued external financing and electoral pressure.

## Forward Market Significance

Revised U.S. first-quarter productivity and unit labor costs are due at 08:30 ET on June 4. The preliminary estimates showed productivity rising at a 0.8% annualized pace and unit labor costs increasing 2.3%. Revisions will determine whether recent wage growth is being supported by additional output or adding more directly to inflation pressure.

Initial jobless claims arrive at the same time, following an initially reported 215,000 for the week ended May 23. The release is the final high-frequency labor check before payrolls and will be especially important after ADP’s stronger gain, the services surveys’ contracting employment measures and the Beige Book’s low-hire, low-fire description.

The May employment report on June 5 remains the main test of the Treasury repricing. Payrolls were expected to increase 93,000 after 115,000, while unemployment was previously 4.3% and average hourly earnings had risen 0.2% on the month and 3.6% from a year earlier. Hiring breadth, unemployment, hours and wages will determine whether the weak services-employment measures outweigh the stabilization suggested by ADP and job openings.

The RBI also decides policy on June 5 after its three-day meeting. The repo rate stands at 5.25% with a neutral stance. The decision must balance imported energy inflation, rupee and funding pressure, and the shift from corporate bonds into bank loans against the growth cost of additional restraint.

On June 8, the New York Fed’s consumer survey will update household inflation expectations after April readings of 3.6% at one year, 3.1% at three years and 3.0% at five years. That evidence bears directly on Logan’s concern that prolonged above-target inflation could become entrenched and on Williams’s expectation that second-round effects may remain contained.

Treasury supply then moves from announcement to execution. The 3-year note auction is scheduled for June 9, with $58 billion expected under the unchanged-size policy, and a 10- to 20-year liquidity-support buyback may accept as much as $2 billion the same afternoon. The reopened 10-year note auction follows on June 10, with $39 billion expected after formal terms are announced.

May CPI, also due June 10 at 08:30 ET, is the decisive inflation release before the June 16-17 FOMC meeting. April headline inflation was 0.6% on the month and 3.8% from a year earlier, while core inflation was 0.4% and 2.8%. The split among energy, shelter and other core services will determine whether the June 3 rise in real yields remains primarily an activity and policy-path adjustment or develops into a broader increase in inflation compensation.

section_summaries.market_read: Investors raised the real policy and growth burden rather than demanding more 10-year inflation compensation.
section_summaries.summary: Treasury yields rose across the curve as stronger services demand, resilient private hiring and higher oil maintained the risk of further Fed tightening. The selloff was led by real yields, while long-term inflation compensation declined and the curve steepened only modestly. Contracting services-employment measures and disagreement between Logan and Williams kept the session from becoming a simple renewed-overheating story.

section_summaries.market_read: The 10-year yield increase came through real rates, extending a month-long pattern despite higher oil and elevated price indexes.
section_summaries.summary: ISM services activity and new orders accelerated, ADP reported 122,000 private-sector jobs and April factory orders rose 4.8%, showing that demand and production backlogs remained firm. Inventories made an unusually large contribution, while ISM employment stayed below 50 and S&P Global reported only marginal services growth and the fastest job shedding since May 2020. The shared signal was that weak hiring had not yet produced a clean reduction in business cost pressure.

section_summaries.market_read: The policy disagreement turns on whether current rates are restrictive enough to finish the inflation adjustment.
section_summaries.section_title: Fed Officials Split Over the Need for Another Increase
section_summaries.summary: Logan argued that accommodative financial conditions, resilient demand and an underlying inflation trend near the mid-2% range could require a rate increase later in 2026. Williams saw policy in the right place and preferred to wait as energy prices, services inflation and the labor market evolved. The Beige Book supported both concerns, showing modest activity and broad energy-cost pass-through alongside stable employment, weaker spending and customer resistance to price increases.

section_summaries.next_check: June 4 announcements will confirm sizes and settlement terms for the next 3-year, 10-year, 30-year and bill sales.
section_summaries.section_title: Treasury Operations Absorb Front- and Long-End Supply
section_summaries.summary: Treasury’s $69 billion 119-day bill sale drew a 3.15 bid-to-cover ratio and showed no sign of funding stress, though no when-issued reference was available to assess the pricing. Treasury also accepted the full $2 billion in its long-end liquidity buyback from $21.26 billion offered, absorbing a small amount of off-the-run duration without indicating market disorder. June 4 announcements will set the next coupon and bill supply terms.

section_summaries.market_read: Energy inflation is encouraging tighter policy in Japan and emerging markets even as growth signals weaken elsewhere.
section_summaries.section_title: Asia and Europe Confront Different Growth-Inflation Mixes
section_summaries.summary: Ueda said the BOJ should discuss raising rates if inflation risks continue to outweigh the Middle East conflict’s growth damage, placing a June move under consideration as the yen weakened. Australia’s growth slowed despite strong data-center investment, China’s services activity accelerated with limited cost pass-through, and euro-area activity contracted as price pressures strengthened. India’s shift from bonds to bank loans lowered corporate borrowing costs but intensified deposit and funding pressure before the RBI decision.

section_summaries.market_read: Broader AI financing channels support investment but increase sensitivity to spreads that assume borrowers will grow into their debt.
section_summaries.next_check: Whether Zambia begins creditor talks and passes the IMF debt-sustainability test remains unresolved.
section_summaries.section_title: Credit Supply Broadens as Sovereign Negotiations Advance
section_summaries.summary: AI-linked borrowing exceeded $370 billion since the start of 2025 and expanded into municipal prepaid-energy financing through Alphabet’s planned $1 billion transaction. Swiss institutions prepared to stop buying bonds from several major oil producers as holdings mature. Zambia moved toward possible talks with creditors blocking its bond repurchase, while Argentina exceeded its gross dollar-purchase target but retained only limited usable net reserves.

June 4 productivity, labor-cost and jobless-claims data provide the last checks before the June 5 employment report, the main test of whether weak services hiring outweighs stronger ADP and job-openings evidence. The RBI also decides policy on June 5, the New York Fed updates inflation expectations on June 8, and Treasury supply follows on June 9-10. May CPI on June 10 will show whether the real-yield repricing broadens into higher inflation compensation before the FOMC meeting.

overall_summary.headline: Real yields drive Treasury selloff as services demand and oil preserve tightening risk
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries sold off broadly on June 3 as stronger U.S. services demand, resilient private hiring and another rise in oil prices preserved the possibility of further Fed tightening. The 2-year yield rose 3.9 basis points to 4.083%, the 5-year added 4.7 basis points to 4.217%, the 10-year climbed 5.2 basis points to 4.496% and the 30-year increased 3.6 basis points to 4.993%.

The adjustment was led by real rates rather than higher long-term inflation compensation: the 10-year real yield rose 6.1 basis points to 2.104%, while the 10-year breakeven fell 0.9 basis point to 2.392%. ADP reported 122,000 private-sector jobs, and the ISM services index rose to 54.5 as activity and new orders strengthened. Yet ISM employment remained in contraction, and a softer S&P Global survey recorded the fastest services job shedding since May 2020. Oil gains and elevated services-price measures kept that demand resilience consequential for policy.

Lorie Logan said rates may need to rise later in 2026 because inflation appeared headed toward the mid-2% range and financial conditions remained accommodative. John Williams saw policy as appropriately calibrated and no immediate need to move either way. Outside the U.S., Kazuo Ueda placed a June BOJ increase under consideration as he judged inflation risks more immediate than the damage to growth. The close preserved tightening concern without signaling a generalized flight from risk, leaving U.S. payrolls and CPI to determine whether weak employment evidence can outweigh firm demand and persistent price pressure.
overall_summary.summary: Services strength, resilient private hiring and renewed oil gains pushed the 10-year Treasury yield 5.2 basis points higher to 4.496%, but contracting employment measures and a split between Fed officials left payrolls and inflation as the decisive tests.
